newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albanians to hand in arms by Sept or face jail.
newsitem.headline: Albanians to hand in arms by Sept or face jail.

text.p: Albanians who looted weapons from military barracks after violence and lawlessness hit the Balkan country in March have been ordered to hand in all arms by September 30, a newspaper reported on Sunday.
Daily Koha Jone said both the defence and interior ministers issued the order and that those who failed to obey would face a sentence of up to five years in jail.
"All kinds of weapons now in the hands of citizens should be returned to police stations and army depots within 45 days, otherwise they (citizens) risk a five-year jail term," it said.
More than 1,500 people have been killed in Europe's most impoverished country since the collapse of bogus investment schemes triggered widespread anarchy.
An estimated one million weapons are in private hands.
The plan foresees that heavy weapons should be turned in by the end of this month, while guns, rifles, grenades and bullets must be handed in no later than September 30.
Neither the defence nor interior ministries were available for comment.

In the last week Albanian police have launched a major crackdown on criminal gangs roaming the Balkan country, taking control of main towns and roads linking the capital Tirana with the rest of the country.
The police have also been gathering huge military arsenals.
Interior Minister Neritan Ceka told state-run television late on Saturday the police were determined to go to the bitter end to restore peace and stability.
Disarming the population is a top priority of Prime Minister Fatos Nano's ruling coalition, which toppled the Democratic Party of former president Sali Berisha in June elections.

The international community, which helped Albania stage the elections, has made clear it would continue assistance if the Socialist-led coalition restores order, improves human rights and adopts sound economic policies.
